thread.title: 3M: The 'Perfect' Investment That Will Dominate The Next Decade (Dividend Sensei) - 3M Company (NYSE:MMM)

author: Brian Bain
title: 3M: The 'Perfect' Investment That Will Dominate The Next Decade (Dividend Sensei) - 3M Company (NYSE:MMM)
text:
The story behind the interview: Dividend Sensei continues to create great content on Seeking Alpha and we recently sat down to discuss a recent article on 3M ( MMM ).
For those who prefer to read, my full interview notes are copied below.
Link to Dividend Sensei's original article: 4 Reasons 3M Could Crush The Market Over The Next Decade
Interview notes: 3M is a Dividend Aristocrat. Actually, it’s a Dividend King defined as growing dividend for 50+ years (59 for 3M)
Dividend growth stocks outperform over time and 3M is a great example of this.
Aristocrats have earned 10.4% since 2000 and S&P was 5.4% with 30% lower volatility.
Companies like Coke (NYSE: KO ), etc. are seeing slower growth while boosting yield
Last 30 years 3M has produced 12.3% per year and market was 10.5% for that time. Can 3M keep doing this at its current size?
Adam applied the Gordon dividend growth model to answer this question.
Analysts are predicting 9.6% earnings growth over next decade and add that to yield 12.2%
Management has a goal of 8-11%. Long-term plan is to maintain past growth
Overtime valuations tend to be mean-reverting. This is why Adam likes to use 10-year periods for analysis.
3M is super diversified and sells over 60,000 in over 200 countries
Most of the sales are on the industrial side. The company has $33 billion in annual sales.
What are 3M’s growth catalysts?
Industrials grow slightly faster than the global economy. ~4-5% per year.
Working on components on EV batteries
Data centers (mobile growth, 5G rollout, IoT, self-driving cars)
3M is the quintessential pick and shovel company
Air and water filtration systems for India
Has its hands in huge global infrastructure growth
Make the high end, mission-critical components for many of these areas
Has been working with many customers for 50+ years. Sits down with customers and asks “what do you need that we can create a solution for?” The company has great pricing power.
The biggest competitive advantage is its R&D
Google (NASDAQ: GOOG ) (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) is famous for allowing engineers to spend 10% working on side projects. 3M allows 15%.
The company is generating 3K patents per year. 3M is a highly efficient R&D company (2 nd most efficient in the world to Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ))
For every dollar it spent in 2016 the company made $9 in gross profits in 2017. The other top 10 companies average $5.50.
3M has laser-like focus and efficiency in R&D
3M has a corporate culture that supports R&D. Company culture heavily focuses on R&D.
3M is excellent at capital allocation
Leadership has long-term experience in the company which creates amazing consistency. It has a very deep leadership bench.
Management is what creates this amazing culture and company
Risk factors for 3M
Industrials are cyclical. 50% of revs are from “fast consumables” which creates recurring rev. Other 50% is more traditional and will rise and fall with the economy.
Dividends are safe, but share price will rise and fall
Currency risk, 60% of sales are global
Over time currencies tend to be mean-reverting and can create headwinds or tailwinds in the short term
Raw material costs could fluctuate and impact margins
Risks of a trade war and additional tariffs with China and Europe
